items.title: NALSAR Convocation row: No inquiry, proceedings closed says BCI Chairman Manan Kumar Mishra
items.summary: Bar Council of India (BCI) Chairman Manan Kumar Mishra has stated that the Council has decided to close proceedings against graduating students at NALSAR University of Law, Hyderabad. Mishra has said that the decision follows representations and reactions of Senior Advocates, members of the bar, law students, and public spirited citizens. "After considering the representations and reactions of Senior Advocates, learned members of the Bar, law students and public spirited citizens, and being satisfied that the 2026 batch of NALSAR, Hyderabad, had no role in any disturbance or movement, the Bar Council of India has decided to close the proceedings altogether. No further action is required from NALSAR." Wishing the students best for their careers, he said, "A word of wisdom: we take immense pride in our legal institutions, and the day you enrol, you become vanguards. Voice your opinions freely, but with respect and institutional decorum. The highest judicial office is our collective pride. Dissent is welcome in a democracy; public ridicule of it is often counterproductive.” The statement follows two circulars by BCI on the evening on August 13, and a press release issued by NALSAR VC

items.title: Convocation row: NALSAR Executive Council to decide whether BCI-mandated inquiry is permissible under University rules
items.summary: National Academy of Legal Studies and Research (NALSAR) University of Law, Hyderabad will refer to its Executive Council the Bar Council of India's (BCI) demand for an inquiry report on the CJI Surya Kant convocation row . The University's response follows two circulars from BCI on August 13. The BCI first barred the entire 2026 batch from being enrolled as advocates. The second circular, passed within hours of the first, reversed the decision but retained the demand for an inquiry report on the persons instrumental in initiating, organising, or mobilising the campaign to protest the invitation of the CJI to the convocation. Vice Chancellor (VC) Srikrishna Deva Rao has said that NALSAR would first examine, under its governance regulations, whether such an inquiry is a constitutional exercise of its powers. "Given the nature of the request, the University will have to consider whether conducting such an inquiry will be a constitutional exercise of its powers. items.title: BCI withdraws order barring enrolment of NALSAR 2026 batch students over campaign against CJI Surya Kant
items.summary: The Bar Council of India (BCI) has withdrawn its order to halt the enrolment of students of the 2026 batch of NALSAR, Hyderabad found to be behind the campaign opposing the participation of Chief Justice of India Justice Surya Kant in the institution's convocation. The new circular issued by BCI Chairman Manan Kumar Mishra within hours of the earlier communication states that members of the BCI debated the move to halt enrolments. "After thorough discussion the Members are of the unanimous view that as per the latest report, vast majority of the students of NALSAR (2026 pass out students) are innocent and they were not inclined to take part in the move of disrespect. Accordingly, the Council modifies the order of Chairman with regard to the ban on the enrolment of the NALSAR Students with the State Bar Councils. All the students will be entitled to get enrolled with the State Bar Councils of their choice," the BCI said. items.title: A Fundamental Right
items.summary: With its new law that makes education a fundamental right with effect from April 1, 2010, India joins a small group of countries with such a statutory provision. All children in the 6 to 14 age group can exercise the right under the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009. An estimated one crore children who do not go to school now are expected to benefit.

items.title: Bengaluru: EPFO official’s death triggers anger over road conditions
items.summary: A 32-year-old central government employee with the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) in Bengaluru was killed on Wednesday, August 12, following a vehicle accident while travelling to work. Medha Akarsh from Kerala, was riding pillion with her colleague on a two-wheeler on Ananth Nagar Main Road, near Electronics City Phase II, when she met with the mishap. According to reports , a car ahead suddenly braked after a pedestrian moved towards the middle of the road. The two-wheeler rider also braked, causing the scooter to skid on a slushy, damaged stretch of road. Medha was thrown onto the road and into the path of an approaching mini goods vehicle. She was rushed to a private hospital but succumbed to her injuries. The mishap occurred around 3 km from her home, reports said. She leaves behind her husband and three-year-old son. Following the accident, residents blamed the poor condition of the road for the mishap. According to a Times of India report , residents said the stretch had remained in poor condition for years, with potholes, waterlogging and damaged road surfaces making daily commuting hazardous.
